known_parity_gaps: Citation digit runs: Python re \d matches Unicode category Nd (e.g. U+0661); Rust accepts ASCII digits only — parity not required for those citations.
RefusalRationale with a non-str rationale: Python __post_init__ raises ValueError; Rust RefusalRationale::try_new takes &str — parity not required for that branch.
REFUSAL_CODES: Python frozenset iteration order is not a contract; vectors record sorted membership only — parity not required on iteration order.
refusal_rationale_for: Python returns Optional; invalid rows fail at import. Rust returns Result because a bad registered row must not become None — parity on that API shape is not required here.

rows.rationale: multiple plausible session heads cannot be disambiguated without inventing session lineage; choosing one would silently rewrite structure
non-monotonic timestamps may reflect legitimate clock skew or source ordering; rewriting timestamps or reordering records would fabricate causal timing data
secret-shaped material requires credential rotation and operator-side removal; rewriting or redacting the persisted record would mutate evidence without revoking the exposed credential
interleaved writer markers are forensic evidence of concurrent writers, not a defect to edit out; rewriting markers or reordering records would fabricate provenance
a size outlier is evidence, not a defect; dropping or truncating the oversized record would destroy data the tool cannot judge
orphan result may be the sole evidence of a completed external action; conservative repair refuses to delete it or synthesize a matching call
conflicting tool-call IDs admit multiple incompatible resolutions; choosing one would invent pairing semantics
reversed call/result order may encode provider or adapter semantics; reordering would rewrite record order without proof
cross-branch pairing concerns lineage and execution ownership; relinking would rewrite branch structure without evidence
provider adjacency rules are defined by the selected replay profile; generic repair cannot know deployment provider semantics
rows.salvage_path: re-run 'sesslint check {path} --profile <id>' matching the deployment provider

rows.rationale: checkpoint/history divergence requires runtime continuation semantics owned by the upstream runtime, which SessLint must not replace
accepted terminal output durability cannot be reconstructed; repair risks duplicate model execution or losing accepted evidence
external side-effect status cannot be determined from session data; abstention is mandatory under every repair policy
unsupported format version must not be approximated by the nearest known schema version
rows.salvage_path: export the session via a supported adapter version or upgrade SessLint, then re-run 'sesslint check {path}'

rows.rationale: unknown critical record may carry identity, parentage, pairing, continuation, or compaction semantics; discarding or rewriting it would require guessing
usage counters are accounting evidence; correcting a divergent total would require knowing which side of the ledger is corrupt
coverage claims cannot be repaired by guessing which span a summary truly covers; fabricating a pointer would invent lineage
a durable-prefix violation is a vendor resume-contract failure; dropping the non-durable tail or synthesizing missing fields would edit evidence to match a contract the file never satisfied
context pressure is advisory evidence against a declared window; truncating or dropping content to buy headroom would destroy the very context the operator needs to checkpoint
snapshot divergence means two vendor-written claims disagree; choosing the authoritative one would edit evidence toward a contract the file never satisfied
duplicated keys admit multiple incompatible resolutions; choosing the winning value would invent record semantics
mid-file schema drift means two schema generations may coexist; normalizing one record's schema would invent which generation it belongs to
a foreign-shape record is only provable against a cited replay vocabulary; rewriting it to the expected shape would discard provider-persisted fields and invent record semantics
rows.salvage_path: the vendor-documented manual path rewrites the offending field to the replay vocabulary's expected value after backup - SessLint performs no rewrite

rows.rationale: unrecognized metadata is advisory; its semantics are not a basis for rewriting or discarding a vendor record
a missing or ambiguous resume target means the real predecessor file is unknown; fabricating a link target would invent lineage
session-index divergence is vendor metadata drift, not ledger corruption; rewriting, rebuilding, or deleting the vendor index would mutate agent-owned state SessLint must not touch
rows.salvage_path: the session file is intact and explicit-ID resume may still work; back up then remove the stale vendor index to force a vendor rebuild - SessLint performs no deletion or mutation
